prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: A story of the 2008 financial crisis, from the US housing boom and subprime mortgages to securitization, the fall of Lehman Brothers and the government response. It shows how a chain of risky choices turned a housing problem into a global crisis.

beats.narration: One broken housing market nearly broke the world economy. How did loans on ordinary homes bring down giant banks? The story starts with a boom that felt like it could never end.
In the early 2000s, US house prices kept rising. Buying a home looked like a sure bet. Lenders were eager to make loans, and many families wanted a piece of the dream.

To keep loans flowing, lenders began approving subprime mortgages: loans to borrowers with weak credit. Many had low starting payments that rose later. It worked only as long as home prices kept climbing.

Then came securitization. Banks bundled thousands of mortgages together and sold slices to investors around the world. Lenders no longer held the risk, so they cared less about whether loans could be repaid.
Then house prices stopped rising and began to fall. Borrowers could not afford their higher payments, and could not sell or refinance. Defaults rise, and securities lose value.

beats.narration: Banks and investors held those securities everywhere, so the losses spread. Nobody knew who was safe, and banks stopped lending to each other. Fear froze the system.
In September 2008, Lehman Brothers, a major investment bank, collapsed. It was one of the largest bankruptcies in history. Panic hit markets worldwide, and the crisis became global.

props.image_query: Wall Street New York stock exchange

beats.narration: Governments and central banks stepped in. The US government rescued banks and key firms, and the Federal Reserve cut interest rates and pumped in money to keep credit moving.
Even so, millions lost jobs and homes, and the economy fell into a deep recession. Recovery was slow, and many families felt the damage for years.
So what caused it? Easy credit, risky loans, and risk passed along until nobody saw it. When trust in housing broke, the system broke too.

props.text: When trust in housing broke, the whole system broke.
